description: Canonical-form vectors (D3): SHA-256 over JCS-compatible serialization (sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace, minimal escaping, UTF-8) of the object minus `annotations`. Pre-normalization rule (D3.3): structurally OPTIONAL arrays/objects with zero elements MUST be absent - their presence is a validation error, so canonicalization never sees them; structurally REQUIRED fields remain even when empty. Decimals are canonical strings (D3.4), never IEEE floats. The number domain (D3.9, NUMBER-1): a JSON number is an integer in plain digits, of magnitude at most 2^53 - 1 - no fraction, no exponent, no -0. A vector with `number-text` carries a JSON TEXT (a vector file cannot carry 1.0 as a number: its own parser has read it already); an implementation reports it valid or invalid, and for a valid text its canonical form equals `canonical-text`. The rule rejects and never rewrites.

vectors.name: utf16-code-unit-key-ordering-not-codepoint
vectors.note: RFC 8785 §3.2.3 orders members by UTF-16 code units: U+1F600 serializes as the surrogate pair D83D DE00, whose first unit (0xD83D) sorts BEFORE U+FB01 — the reverse of code-point order. Two tools MUST derive identical digests (D3.4); this vector is the P9b-3 regression guard.

vectors.name: empty-omission-optional-array-present-is-error
vectors.reason: structurally optional array `relations` present with zero elements - MUST be omitted before serialization (D3.3; the omitted-vs-empty hash-fragmentation corpse)

vectors.name: empty-omission-required-array-stays
vectors.reason: `members` is structurally REQUIRED on RequirementSet - it remains even when empty; only optional empties are omitted (measured live: the C5 GC domain Set)

vectors.name: number-integers-in-plain-digits
vectors.reason: the whole domain is written one way: an optional minus and digits

vectors.name: number-largest-magnitude
vectors.reason: 2^53 - 1 on both sides: the largest integers every IEEE double holds exactly, with its neighbours

vectors.name: number-like-text-inside-strings-is-text
vectors.reason: the rule reads number tokens, not digits: a key or a string value may say 1.0, even after an escaped quote

vectors.name: number-one-beyond-the-range
vectors.reason: 2^53: exact in a double, but its successor is not - the range ends one below

vectors.name: number-reported-9007199254740993
vectors.reason: the reported case: JavaScript reads it as 9007199254740992, Python exactly - two digests, two verdicts

vectors.name: number-twenty-digits
vectors.reason: compared as text: no implementation needs big integers to refuse it

vectors.name: number-fraction-zero
vectors.reason: a second spelling of 1 - one tool hashes 1.0, another 1; rejected, never rewritten (D3.4)

vectors.name: number-negative-zero
vectors.reason: a second spelling of 0, and the one a parser that keeps integers cannot see

vectors.name: number-fraction
vectors.reason: a fraction is a decimal, and a decimal is a string (D3.4)

vectors.name: number-nested
vectors.reason: every number of the text, at any depth

vectors.name: number-in-annotations-too
vectors.reason: the rule is on the file, not on the semantic domain: a tool checks it without knowing where annotations are
